Definition: a tamarisk tree; by extension, a grove of any kind
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture means a tamarisk tree, the word is ʼêshel. It appears in Genesis and 1 Samuel, and the meaning does not shift with the setting. Nothing about it is fancy; it simply names what it names.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʼêshel earns its place in a study like this — it carries real weight in the passages above. That is the sense I carry into the passages above.
RelatedEvents: Saul's Death at Gilboa; The Priests of Nob Massacred
